text: The Science: Your neurons have "brakes" called KCNQ channels, which keep a neuron from firing over and over by letting potassium out of it. Stress does lower the potassium in your blood, since adrenaline pushes it into your cells (Brown, et al, 1983), but with less potassium outside them, nerve cells rest farther from firing, not closer (Kuwabara, et al, 2002).
reader: someone with trauma or in withdrawal who is anxious, wired, numb or foggy, following the protocol's diet and electrolyte steps and wanting to know why each one is there
